_about: Read by `ghostwriter.py fund` and the occasional thank-you line. cost_usd = the AI it took to build Ghost Writer, at API list price, and it is the one collective goal: once raised_usd reaches it, the line stops for good. Numbers are refreshed from the maintainer's build ledger. value_moments are the only points where the line may appear.

value_moments.when: the book leaves the research phase with every exit criterion met (`phase advance` research -> synthesis, no override)
value_moments.why: A finished research phase (the author's own exit criteria ticked, coverage at the threshold, every citation with an honest status) is the first thing the author holds that they could not get from a chatbot: a defensible research base for the book.

value_moments.when: the first time a chapter draft passes all 3 checks (tournament or promote)
value_moments.why: A chapter that is sourced, sounds like the author and survives its strongest objection is the first finished piece of the book the author is holding.

value_moments.when: every chapter in the spine has been promoted
value_moments.why: A complete, gate-passing draft of the whole book is the full payoff the author came for.

value_estimates._about: Assumptions behind the 'hours of drafting you didn't do' line. It is an ESTIMATE, always labeled as one, and deliberately low. `ghostwriter.py fund` prints this math. Edit the numbers here, not in code.
value_estimates.label: estimate
value_estimates.formula: words in the passing chapter / baseline_words_per_hour x claim_share, rounded down; full draft = the same on all promoted chapters' words; under 10 minutes = no value claim

per_moment.chapter-passed: words in the passing chapter (the shortest passing run, at a tournament)
per_moment.full-draft: sum of words in every promoted chapter in the spine
per_moment.research-ready: no hours claim: there is no published benchmark for research time we would trust, so the line names the outcome only

benchmarks.claim: Composing text at a keyboard averaged 19.0 words per minute (about 1,140 words per hour); transcribing averaged 32.5.
benchmarks.source: Karat, Halverson, Horn & Karat (1999), 'Patterns of entry and correction in large vocabulary continuous speech recognition systems', CHI '99.
benchmarks.checked: citation confirmed (24 users, speech vs keyboard, transcription and composition tasks); the 19.0/32.5 wpm figures via Wikipedia 'Words per minute', which cites this paper

why_conservative: the benchmark is raw composing speed in a short lab session, faster than real book drafting: a sourced chapter also needs research, structure and revision, which it leaves out
only half of the hours that fast pace implies are claimed
hours are rounded down, and the shortest passing draft is used
the research-ready moment makes no time claim at all

_about_hook: hook_match is read by the OPT-IN Claude Code hook scripts/fund_line_hook.py: when an agent runs the CLI through the Bash tool (not a terminal), the CLI prints a neutral '[value moment]' marker with no money in it, and the hook shows the line to the user as a systemMessage, under the same caps and state.
